title: Bell tests for collider decay processes
authors: Danilo M. Fucci, Alexandre C. Orthey, Alan J. Barr, Christopher G. Timpson
abstract: We propose Bell tests for collider decays using independently sampled analysis axes as settings and detector regions to assign binary or null outcomes. We show that a Bell violation requires postselection, opening a loophole. However, under measurement independence and operational equivalence of acceptance events across settings, any local model exploiting the loophole must be nonclassical in the sense of measurement contextuality. We derive a Bell inequality violated by singlet correlations when the effective spin-analyzing powers are sufficiently high. Its violation then witnesses Bell nonlocality or measurement contextuality.
summary: This work proposes a novel Bell test framework for analyzing data from particle collider decays. It tackles the inherent loophole caused by postselection by requiring operational equivalence across measurement settings. A violation of the derived Bell inequality provides evidence for quantum nonlocality or measurement contextuality in this high-energy physics context.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to perform Bell tests using data recorded from high-energy collider decays, addressing the challenge of measurement settings being determined by detector acceptance rather than freely chosen.
main_result: A violation of a derived Bell inequality, under assumptions of measurement independence and operational equivalence, witnesses either Bell nonlocality or joint-acceptance contextuality.
method: The authors derive a continuous-input Bell inequality and analyze the loophole opened by postselection, showing that operational equivalence constrains local hidden variable models.
model_or_system: The system involves the decay of unstable qubits in a collider, where daughter momenta act as spin analyzers. The test uses independently sampled analysis axes to define accepted spherical caps for binary outcomes.
key_observables: The Bell functional B = -<x . y a b>, the local acceptance probability q_A, and the joint acceptance event D.
important_parameters: Spin-analyzing power (eta_A), the cap radius (phi), and the bound violation condition mu_A mu_B > 3/4.
main_assumptions: Measurement independence (lambda-independence) and the operational equivalence of joint-acceptance events across all settings are crucial assumptions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the geometric coarse-graining defined by the analysis axis, showing the accepted caps (+1, -1) and the no-click region (empty set).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the Bell test framework for collider data, addressing the postselection loophole, deriving the contextuality constraint via operational equivalence, and finally presenting the specific Bell inequality and its quantum prediction.
why_interesting: While focused on particle physics, the rigorous development of contextuality constraints based on operational equivalence in a measurement setting is highly relevant to foundational quantum information theory and loophole-free tests.
